name: beatZIG gen2
movedFrom: Until 2026-11-09 this CPU was cpus/release/gen2.mjs (named gen2), with its parts in cpus/release/gen2/. Only the names and the places changed.
what: The beatZIG line, generation 2: a small network (features v4, one hidden layer of 32) scores the moves; a reader ("one", k=2) looks at the two best by score on re-drawn states and picks the one whose state after the move is evaluated higher. Learned from a deep look-ahead CPU and a looking-ahead CPU, a language model (Haiku 5.5) on the hard decisions, and a person's marks on the model's moves.

frozenCode.note: The CPU module imports only the copies in its own folder; cpus/learned/ and the others may change without changing how it plays. sha256 of each file with line endings read as LF; all = sha256 of the hashes in the order listed.

reader.note: the state right after the move, evaluated (gen2/beatZIG/eval.mjs: a hand-made evaluation, not learned), averaged over 2 re-drawn states; a move the sim cannot play (a spell, an effect) is played as it is when it is the best by score

learnedFor.note: The rules the data was played under. When the game's rules change (the first-turn draw, a card, a rule version), the data and this CPU are of the old rules: learn it again.

validation.note: whole matches kept apart (20%); the share of decisions where the CPU's best move is the teacher's

records.teacher: deep (the best few moves played out through the rest of the turn and the other side's turn)
records.what: deep against simple, both seat orders, every pair of the 7 start decks, seeds 301-303
lookahead against lookahead and against simple, seeds 101-105
a student CPU against simple and lookahead, both seat orders, seeds 401-405; every decision of the student labelled by lookahead

records.teacher: Haiku 5.5 (hard decisions only: installs, executions, what lookahead leaves to the game's CPU)
records.what: the 40 matches picked out of the 980 (lost, many differences, weak decks, many moves the sim cannot read); 759 calls, $0.414; each answer weighted by a machine judgement of which move is worth more

records.teacher: a person (指揮, for 文豪)
records.what: adopted 29 (the model's move taken), corrected to the right move 12, the teacher's move taken 39

method.loss: softmax over the candidates of a decision

evaluation.note: Strength = the share of matches won, both seat orders, every pair of start decks, game b8214a6; 95% range: Wilson. Measured with the file under the name cpus/release/gen2.mjs, before it moved here (the same measure again under the final name: 288-202 against gen1): the reader's re-drawn states follow the match name, so under another file name some matches play out differently (1 of 49 in a check under the final name), the strength is the same.

vsGen1.note: the same CPU under the name cpus/forged-g2-one2.mjs, when it was picked

evaluation.repeatability: In a clean clone of the commit that froze it (nothing uncommitted), with cpus/learned/ (policy, network, loop guard) and cpus/topk-core.mjs deliberately broken, it played 98 matches against gen1 (seed 1, both orders) identically to the measurement it was picked by: 98/98. After the move to this place, played again under the old names (temporary wrappers): 98 of 98 identical to the first measurement (the temporary wrappers imported the parts from this place).

timePerDecision.note: choose() of the CPU, with the reader; the CPU against itself, a quiet machine, 12 matches; the time includes the bench opening the sim (re-drawing the hidden cards), which a device would do in its own way. Milliseconds.

playsOnly: what the seat can see (its own query) and the states the reader re-draws of what it cannot see; no hidden information of the other side.
